title: axis — one (configuration, axis) constraint from S3 (4.5.2)

caller_id.description: <qid>:v<N>:<config>:<axis>, issued by the fan-out launcher, never chosen by the sub-agent (4.3.1). The revision is part of the id because the id is also the server's isolation unit: without it the same axis at two revisions shares one session context, and a re-run inherits the attempt it exists to replace. Revision 1 writes v1 rather than omitting it -- an implicit default is the shape that has already caught five rules here. The form without v<N> is accepted while the cards that predate a6dca6a migrate, and stops being accepted after.

kb_version.description: pinned by S3.0; every sibling cites the same one (check 33)

method.description: deterministic output takes computed: sources, an estimate takes assumed: (4.5.2)

inequalities.description: One entry per inequality this axis owns, derived from 4.5.3 rather than declared here. It exists because `abstain_reason` is one string and an axis owns several inequalities: folding seven verdicts into one sentence makes prose, and prose is what 4.5.2.1 replaced. The failure it prevents is specific -- an axis that says nothing about two of its five inequalities reads as 'this axis does not constrain there', and S4 cannot tell that from 'this axis could not compute'. An interval with neither min nor max is not a way around it; that is the silence itself.

state.description: Four, and never folded into fewer. Merging `abstained` with `failed` makes an axis that honestly reported no grounds (P5) look like one that died, and the first is normal while the second must stop the plan.

kind.description: Why there is no interval, and the three are a field rather than a sentence because the next action differs: measure something, write down that it does not bind here, or nothing at all. A sentence loses that distinction and the reader has to guess it back.

missing.description: Named inputs that were absent. Required when kind is no_input: naming them is the difference between a gap someone can close and a shrug.

then.$comment: Exactly one of the three. A returned bound must say something, and what it says comes in three shapes: a numeric range, a discrete set of permitted values, or a requirement on the plan. oneOf and not anyOf because two of them on one inequality is two bounds wearing one entry, and S4 would intersect the pair it recognised and drop the other.

counterexample.description: required when verdict is infeasible: which value exceeds which limit (P5)
